רותאלרזעלתהלארץמאנגליהכצעירהבשנת1954היאל: Ruth Elraz immigrated to Israel from England as a young woman in 1954. She studied social work at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and sculpture in London, Paris, and Jerusalem.
רותיהיתהשילובשלאשאהבהכעסלהטאקטיביסטיומעו: Ruthie was a combination of fire, love, anger, activist fervor, and endless personal and social involvement. She was an adoring mother to her only daughter, Danya, and a grandmother whose love and pride in her grandchildren surprised even her.
רותיעבדהשניםכפסיכותרפיסטיתבשירותיהייעוץל: Ruthie worked for years as a psychotherapist in the Hebrew University’s Student Counseling Services.
בהמשךדרכהרותיהיתהאחתהאימהותהמייסדותשלמרכ: Later on, Ruthie was one of the founding mothers of the Counseling Center for Women.
רותיהייתהאידאליסטיתפמיניסטיתדעתניתושותפה: Ruthie was an idealist, a feminist, opinionated, and a central partner in the formation and determination of the Center’s character; in committees, staff meetings, and in all the spaces where the ethical and professional image of the Counseling Center for Women was formed.
רותהייתהפעילהבמשךשניםבצוותההיגוישלהמרכזו: Ruth was active for years on the Center’s Steering Committee and in the early years was also responsible for finances and salaries.
רותיהיתהמטפלתחדהולאשגרתיתמעוררתהשראה: Ruthie was a sharp and unconventional therapist.
בעלתידעוניסיוןויכולתלניתוחקליניחדאינטליג: She had the knowledge and experience and the ability for an inspiring, intelligent, creative, feminist and in-depth clinical analysis.
רותיהיתההמדריכההמיתולוגיתשלסטודנטיותומטפ: Ruthie was the “mythic supervisor” of many new students and therapists at the CCW. In her practice as a supervisor, she actually raised a new generation of feminist therapists.
כשהלכהברחובמסתברשהיאהכירהאתכלהכלביםבשכונ: When she walked down the street, it turned out she knew all the dogs in the neighborhood, and she would stop to talk with them (and with their owners).
רותיהיתהפעילהבתנועותשלוםאחתהמייסדותשלתנו: Ruthie was an activist. She was one of the founders of the ‘Women in Black’, a women’s peace movement, and was also active in the ‘Israeli Committee Against House Demolition’. She did not leave left-wing politics outside the Center and thought that politics should be an integral part of the Center’s existence and operation as a feminist social-therapeutic organization.
בחוברתהמאמריםשלמרכזיעוץלאשהנשיםבמרחבהטיפ: In the Counseling Center for Women’s book of articles, “Women in the Therapeutic Space” published in 2001, an article was published that Ruthie wrote together with team member Marcia Levin, who wrote “A Meeting with the Other: The Message in the Unspoken Word.” Click here to read.
עדסוףחייהקרובלגיל92אפשרהיהלראותאתרותישבא: Until the end of her life, close to the age of 92, Ruthie (who had green hair in those days) could be seen moving and rolling in her wheelchair at protests and demonstrations on the streets of Jerusalem.
לכלאחתמחברותהמרכזזכרונותמשלהמרותאלרזהחרו: Each of the Center’s members has her own memories of Ruth Elraz, engraved in her memory and heart.

גודיגדלהבוויניפגקנדהבתלמשפחהציונית: Judy grew up in Winnipeg, Canada, the daughter of a Zionist family.
כצעירההגיעהלישראללביקורב1949עםאמהבאותובי: As a young woman she came to visit Israel in 1949 with her mother. During that visit and afterwards she felt that her place was in Israel and felt committed to therapeutic, social and feminist work in Israel.
בשנותה50ו60גודיהתמחתהבמכוןהפסיכואנליטיבי: In the '50s and '60s Judy trained at the Psychoanalytic Institute in Jerusalem, and in 1970 she was part of the team that established the first clinic for psychological therapy.
ב1975היאנסעהלאוניברסיטהבברקליקליפורניהפג: In 1975 she went to the University of Berkeley, California, met her partner Aharon and studied sex therapy, and was a pioneer in bringing the subject to Israel as one of the first therapists in the field of sex therapy.
גודיהיתהפמיניסטיתבכלהווייתהופורצתדרךבכלמ: Judy was a feminist in her whole being and a trailblazer in everything related to viewing the worlds of mental health and sexual health through a gender-feminist lens.
בשנת1986גודיהצטרפהלקולקטיבהנשיםשייסדאתמר: In 1986, Judy joined the collective of women who founded the Counseling Center for Women, a pioneering model of feminist therapy for women in Israel.
גודינשארהחברהיקרהמשמעותיתומוערכתבארגוןעד: Judy remained a dear, meaningful and appreciated member of the organization until her last day. She contributed her spirit, her ideology, her wisdom, her friendship and her love.
לאנרגיותולחיוניותשלגודילאהיוגבולותהיאאהב: Judy's energy and vitality had no limits. She loved to travel the world and kept traveling well into her 90s. She loved to dance and to swim, and did not let age limit her.
כפישכתבהחברתהמיכלשונוברון: As her friend Michal Shonbrun wrote:
שנשמתהורוחהתמשכנהלרקודבגןעדןעםכלהמלאכיםש: "May her soul and spirit continue to dance in paradise, with all the angels above and below.
מאחלותשהכרתהתודהואהבתינואלגודיימשיכולהפר: We wish that the gratitude and our love for Judy will continue to nourish and sustain us on our journeys.
שהנשמהשלהתמשיךלהצמיחזרעייצירהחמלההומניות: May her soul continue to grow seeds of creativity, compassion, humanity and love".
גודיאכןהורישהקצתמרוחהואהבתהלכלמישזכתהלהכ: Judy indeed bequeathed some of her spirit and her love to everyone privileged to know her and work with her.

מרליןהצעירהבמשפחהעםחמישהילדיםנולדהוגדלהב: Marlene, the youngest in a family of five children, was born and raised in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA.
עלתהלישראלבשנת1973עםבןהזוגמוטיושניילדיהה: She immigrated to Israel in 1973 with her husband Moti and their two young children, David and Betty.
מרליןגדלהוהתפתחהעםאמאפמיניסטיתולתחושתההי: Marlene grew up with a feminist mother, and in her own feeling she had always been a feminist.
מרליןלמדהפסיכולוגיהחינוכיתוקליניתוטיפולמ: Marlene studied educational and clinical psychology and family therapy, worked in various therapeutic settings for many years, and was always dedicated to creating a better world.
מרליןהאמינהשנשיםזקוקותלמקוםבטוחלפסיכותרפ: Marlene believed that women needed a safe place for psychotherapy, a feminist women’s space, and so she joined the Counseling Center for Women in 1990, at the second stage of our formation as a leading organization in feminist therapy for women.
המרכזהתאיםבדיוקלמרליןהחכמההנלהבתוהמחויבת: The Center was a perfect fit for the wise, enthusiastic Marlene, committed to ideology and to therapy in a feminist approach.
מרליןעסקהבטיפולפסיכותרפיאישיזוגימשפחתיוק: Marlene engaged in individual, couple, family and group psychotherapy, and supervised in all these fields.
היאתרמהלכולנומהידעוהניסיוןהעשירשלהבנוסףמ: She contributed to all of us from her rich knowledge and experience. In addition, Marlene was one of the first EMDR supervisors in Israel.
בחוברתהמאמריםנשיםבמרחבהטיפולישיצאהלאורבש: In the book of articles "Women in the Therapeutic Space", published in 2001, an article by Marlene was published:
טיפולזוגיוקבוצתתמיכהשלאמהותשורדותהתעללות: "Couples therapy and a support group of mothers who are survivors of sexual abuse".
אניאסירתתודהשהכשרתיבתרפיהפמיניסטיתאפשרהל: "I am grateful that my training in feminist therapy allowed me to listen to women in a fuller way, and to relate to them with all their potential".
במרכזיעוץלאשהמרליןמצאהלעצמהקהילהשלאחיותו: At the Counseling Center for Women, Marlene found for herself a community of sisters and partners on a values-driven and professional journey, and the Counseling Center for Women gained one of our dear mothers.

מודלהשירותהייחודישלנומשתרעמעברלחדרהטיפול: Our unique service model extends beyond the therapy room and into our communities. CCW serves as a knowledge hub and professional training center for students and practitioners alike, enabling us to share our expertise and impact future generations. Each year, social work students from recognized Israeli universities are accepted by the Center to receive personal and professional supervision. The practical training at CCW gives a real-life look into the world of feminist psychotherapy; deepening theoretical knowledge and helping students acquire skills to treat women in crisis and other challenges that may arise during a woman’s life.
בשנת1986תשעפסיכותרפיסטיותחלוצותבתחוםהתאח: In 1986, nine female psychotherapists, all pioneers in their field, joined to form a collective. They had a unique vision to make high-quality, gender-sensitive psychotherapy accessible to all women in Israel.
כיוםהמיזםאותוהגומרכזיעוץלאשהצמחלכדיארגון: Today, the Counseling Center for Women (CCW), as their initiative was called, has grown into a thriving nonprofit organization that serves 300 women annually. It provides 10,000 psychotherapy hours each year from two centers in Jerusalem and Ramat Gan, as well as from satellite clinics.
נשיםבישראלמתמודדותעםמגווןאתגריםוקונפליקט: Women in Israel face distinct challenges and conflicts in their personal and professional lives: inequality in family sphere and workplace, economic disparity, and limited political representation. These difficulties are intensified during times of social and political crisis. As the first and only Israeli nonprofit professional endeavor to offer subsidized psychotherapy services to women, including the underprivileged and those at-risk for various reasons, CCW fills a vital need in thousands of lives.

מרכזהטיפוללנשיםבגישהפמיניסטית: A therapy center for women with a feminist perspective
מרכזהטיפולמציעלפונותאליוטיפולנפשיפרטניזו: The Therapy Center offers its clients individual, couples and group psychotherapy, based on the feminist psychology approach. Feminist psychology is a therapeutic approach that views society as a significant factor influencing a woman's world, her perceptions, choices, aspirations and ability to fulfill herself; and recognizes women's needs and characteristics as worthy of deep understanding and appropriate, tailored attention.
צוותהמטפלותמונהכ30נשותמקצועעובדותסוציאלי: The team of therapists numbers about 30 professionals: clinical social workers, clinical psychologists and psychiatrists, specializing in therapy with women and in the issues characteristic of the psychology of women: relationships, singlehood, sexuality, self-image, body image, trauma, crisis, eating disorders, depression, motherhood, mother-daughter relations, pregnancy and fertility, sexual orientation, women and career, coping with illness and disability, and more.
הטיפולבמרכזיעוץלאשהנעשהתוךשימושבמגווןטכנ: Therapy at the Counseling Center for Women uses a variety of therapeutic techniques and approaches meant to create a secure therapeutic space tailored to the needs of every client; therapy is offered in Hebrew, English, Spanish and additional languages.
הטיפולבמרכזיעוץלאישהמתקייםבשניסניפיםמרכז: Therapy at the Counseling Center for Women takes place at two main branches in Ramat Gan and Jerusalem, as well as at clinics across the country - Pardes Hanna, Modi'in, Kiryat Tivon and the Western Galilee.
התשלוםעבורהטיפולמבוססעלסולםמדורגתוךהתחשב: The fee for therapy is based on a sliding scale, taking into account the economic and family situation of every client, in order to make quality therapy accessible to every woman who seeks it.

מיועדלכלאשההמתמודדתעםסבלכאבאומצוקהרגשיתו: Intended for any woman coping with suffering, pain or emotional distress, it seeks to support the woman who turns to it, help her find her unique inner voice, empower her, recognize her strength, expand her range of choice and freedom, her growth and personal fulfillment, and bring about an improvement in her quality of life, her family life and the community around her.
מטפלותהמרכזהןמומחיותבטיפולבנשיםמכירותלעו: The Center's therapists are experts in treating women, deeply familiar with the difficulties and challenges unique to women, and hold the knowledge and tools suited to treating these difficulties and challenges. מרכזיעוץלאשההואמרכזלטיפולהדרכהוהכשרהותיק: The Counseling Center for Women is a long-standing and unique center for therapy, supervision and training in the treatment of women, which has amassed rich and unique knowledge over the 35 years since its founding in treating women and the unique issues arising from the women's life cycle. Therapy at the Counseling Center for Women is conducted at eye level, from a feminist approach that seeks to connect every woman to her strengths and abilities, while giving respect and space to her culture, background, wishes and aspirations, and from an understanding of the social context in which she lives.
מגווןהשיטותהגישותוהכליםהטיפולייםהמצוייםב: The variety of methods, approaches and therapeutic tools available at the Center under one roof allows every client to find a response to her unique needs and difficulties.

מהיפסיכותרפיהמינחשבתפסיכותרפיסטית: What is psychotherapy? Who is considered a psychotherapist?
הטיפולהפסיכותרפיהמוכרגםבשםטיפולפסיכולוגי: Psychotherapeutic treatment (also known as "psychological therapy") is based on conversations, and its goal is to alleviate the client's mental difficulties and suffering and to help build a more stable, flexible and adaptive mental structure for life's challenges. A psychotherapist is any mental health professional who has undergone training in psychotherapy (a clinical psychologist, clinical social worker, or psychiatrist).

המטפלותבמרכזהןפסיכולוגיותקליניותעובדותסו: The Center's therapists are clinical psychologists, clinical social workers and psychiatrists with training and experience in treating women.

The feminist therapy approach advocated by the Center is integrated into each therapist's own approach. The Center also has therapists certified in unique therapeutic methods such as Gestalt, guided imagery, safe touch, EMDR, hypnosis and NLP.
מהההבדלביןפסיכולוגיתקליניתלעובדתסוציאלית: What is the difference between a clinical psychologist and a clinical social worker?
פסיכולוגיהקליניתועבודהסוציאליתקליניתהןשנ: Clinical psychology and clinical social work are two clinical (therapeutic) specialization tracks with slightly different emphases. Originally, the difference between the fields lay in their approach to the individual's well-being: the psychological approach emphasizes the individual's inner world, while the social approach relates to the social context in which the individual operates. Over the years, however, the differences between the fields have narrowed, especially when it comes to clinically trained mental health professionals who have undergone many varied trainings. The therapists at the Counseling Center for Women, whether psychologists or social workers, have clinical training and focus both on the client's inner world and on the external influences and social context in which she lives.

An inquiry prompted by a specific crisis or a need for focused therapy may find its solution in short-term therapy. Deeper difficulties that accompany our lives over a long time, on the other hand, may require a deeper and more comprehensive therapeutic process and a wider time frame. Part of the therapeutic dialogue is meant to allow each of us to define the nature and scope of the change she wishes to invest in.

אתגורהנחותיסודמגדריותהמטפלתהפמיניסטיתמסי: Challenging basic gender-based assumptions: The feminist therapist helps the client to see the way in which she has internalized negative stereotypes regarding women and femininity. Therapeutic work reduces the pathological view, in that it points to the woman’s strengths, her abilities and her capabilities, and supports an understanding of the need for the defense mechanisms she has used so far. The feminist therapist helps a woman discover the connections between her feelings and behaviors that are preventing her from fulfilling her human potential and her full talents in all areas of life. In this way, the client learns to recognize that the personal is political, contemplates the courage in her inner world, understands herself better, recognizes her strength and thereby broadens her possible choices in various areas of her life.
צמצוםההיררכיהבחדרהטיפוליםאםבחברהובגישותט: Minimizing hierarchy in the therapy session: While hierarchy is widespread in society and in many therapeutic approaches (men in relation to women and the therapist in relation to the client), feminist therapy strives to minimize hierarchy and strengthen the point of view that women share similar life experiences and similar challenges, and that every woman, whether she is a therapist or a client seeking therapy, has significant knowledge and experience. In feminist therapy, the therapist is not perceived as the all-knowing expert; instead, respect is given to the client’s interpretation and knowledge of her own life. Feminist therapy supports the de-mystification and transparency of the therapy process: The therapist explains the method of therapy to the client, as well as her insights into the psychodynamic processes that the client is going through. She may share her feelings with the client, along with incidents from her own personal life, to the extent that she believes this will move the therapeutic process forward.

רבשנותה20המאוחרותשלההתחילהאתהטיפולשלהבמר: R., in her late 20s, began her therapy at the Counseling Center for Women hoping to reduce the intensity of post-traumatic symptoms after experiencing rape in her past. Today she lives with her parents and is in rehabilitation.
התקיפותהמיניותהאלימותוהחטיפותשהתרחשוב7בא: The sexual assaults, violence and kidnappings that took place on October 7, which were widely covered in the media, caused a severe regression in R.'s mental state, after she had been in a stable mental condition before the attack. Following the news reports, R. barely left the house and began suffering from sleep difficulties. The fears, the anxiety and the rape trauma she had been through resurfaced.
במהלךהטיפולבמרכזיעוץלאשהרסיפרהכימצליחהלד: During therapy at the Counseling Center for Women, R. said she manages to talk about her painful experience in a safe space. The trust built between her and her therapist allows her to freely share details about her condition. The feeling that she is not alone calms her and allows her to continue her rehabilitation process. The therapy gives her tools for coping more effectively with emotional challenges.
ישראליםרביםהמתגורריםבסמיכותלגבולמצפוןומד: Many Israelis living near the border, in the north and south, were evacuated from their homes after the October 7 attack. Since then they have been housed in temporary accommodations, including hotels, youth hostels or homes designated by the state. The online support group for women evacuees from the north was established by the Counseling Center for Women and is accompanied by a psychotherapist from the Center, Dr. Rachel Shadletzky-Hart, who is herself evacuated from her home. The group creates a sense of togetherness and allows its members to discuss feelings and experiences that are hard for them to share with other people.
המשתתפותבקבוצהחושבותאומנםכימרביתהאנשיםמב: The group participants believe that while most people understand their situation, they cannot deeply grasp the meaning of being evacuated. Staying far from home and not knowing when they will be able to return makes them feel "groundless" and "dependent" on the goodwill of others. Many participants shared that they feel anxious and very worried that their homes will be destroyed by rockets.
במהלךתשעתהחודשיםמאזשמשפחותיהןפונומבתיהןה: During the nine months since their families were evacuated from their homes, they were moved several times. Each time anew, their children had to adjust to new environments and schools. The children are deeply affected by the ongoing war and some of them need mental health assistance. Many of the participants feel "fed up" and are physically and emotionally exhausted. Some have experienced emotional breakdowns.
הקבוצהמסייעתבמציאתפתרונותמעשייםלדילמותשע: The group helps find practical solutions to dilemmas arising from the evacuees' complex situation. For example, one participant was caring for her sick brother, her elderly mother and her family at the same time. She spoke about the emotional price she pays, alongside the fear of moving to a home of her own and leaving her mother and brother behind. Through the support and encouragement she received from the group, she managed to move and rent a house with her family. Another member of the group was unable to share and accept the fact that she was suffering mentally and needed help; for her, this was considered taboo. With the group's help, she opened up and sought psychiatric assistance. Although the process took time, little by little she began to recover.
